title: Onramp handoff + SDK checkpoints — Nov 4 2025
summary: Sprint checkpoint meeting to align SDK quickstart, sample repo handoff, and docs changes before the November customer onramp. Focus areas: simplify first-run flow, CI flakiness, telemetry opt-out wording, and onboarding checklist for solutions engineering.
attendees: Anika Patel (owner), Marco Li, Sofia Hernandez, Evan Chen, Priya Singh, Jamal Ortiz (notes)
agenda: 1) Quick status on SDK quickstart changes 2) Sample repo handoff readiness 3) Docs copy + legal review items 4) CI/test flakiness and mitigation 5) Action items / owners
notes:
(timeboxed 45m)

Quickstart (TS SDK)
- Marco: landed the auth flow simplification in branch 'onramp/auth-lite'. Reduced steps from 7 -> 4 for first run. Example commands now: `npm init redwood-quickstart && REDWOOD_API_KEY=... npm start`.
- Remaining: swap example to use streaming chat endpoint by default. Need to update samples that assume polling.
- TODO: add small inline snippet in quickstart README that shows `stream.eachChunk(...)` usage. (Priya)
decisions:
- Default quickstart will use hosted 'streaming-chat' route rather than polling.
- Telemetry will be opt-out by default in sample apps, with clear README callout. Legal to review copy (Jamal assigned).
- Sample repo 'redwood-examples/onramp' will be the canonical handoff artifact for solutions eng.
action_items:
1) Priya: write streaming snippet + unit test (due 2025-11-07)
2) Marco: open PR to change quickstart default route to streaming (GITHUB PR linked) (due 2025-11-06)
3) Evan: add a small e2e that runs quickstart in CI using ephemeral API key; isolate token usage to test account (due 2025-11-10)
4) Jamal: coordinate legal review of telemetry copy and post comments in Confluence (DE-1284) (due 2025-11-09)
5) Sofia: create handoff checklist for Solutions Eng with steps, expected artifacts, and rollback notes (due 2025-11-06)
blockers:
- CI flakes: intermittent timeout on sample download step (seen in runner-ubuntu-22). Suspect network/transient. Evan to spike caching of sample archive.
- Model size: some private quickstart configurations require quantized artifacts; we need a small public example route that uses a tiny model for demos (Marco exploring distil variant).
- Legal copy hold on telemetry — cannot ship opt-out language until cleared. This blocks pushing default to main for samples.
follow_up:
- Weekly sync scheduled Friday 10:30am PST; add short demo slot (5 mins) for the streaming quickstart.
- Create short checklist doc 'onramp-handoff-checkpoints.md' under redwood-examples repo (Sofia).
- Track e2e flakiness in JIRA subtask under DE-1284; label 'ci-flake'.
raw_body:
Meeting fragments / notes-to-self:
- 'If time, demo the two-line change to TS client for streaming' — keep it > 2 mins.
- Consider adding a 'first 5 minutes' section to README that includes expected costs, latency, and token estimates so customers don't get surprised.
- Ideas: tiny interactive playground embedded in quickstart that calls the hosted API with demo key (read-only, rate-limited). Security review needed.
- Slack snippets: posted the quickstart gif in #devexp; reactions show confusion around 'set API key' step. People expect a 'web UI' option. Need to call this out in README.

References / commands used during the meeting:
- checkout and run local quickstart: `git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/redwood-examples.git && cd onramp && npm ci && REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxx npm run demo`
- run e2e locally (fast): `npx playwright test quickstart --project=chromium --grep @smoke`

Open questions:
- Do we surface usage/cost estimates for the sample workload in README? (yes, but precise numbers need verification)
- Should we include a one-click cloud run button for the demo? (parking this; product input required)

Status of related PRs: GITHUB PR #4923 (sample readme cleanup) — ready for review but blocked on telemetry copy.

Notes for next sync: capture short video (30s) of the streaming experience to use in handoff. Priya to record and upload to Confluence.
